column1: # Blocks required to stay BUILT. One row per block; the gate reads this file
# and no other (there is no --baseline <path>, design Constraint 6).
# `ordinal`  the block's 1-based position among that page's C# blocks, as
#            `--list` numbers it. Adding a block above it on the page moves it,
#            and the gate says so -- that is the price of an address a reader
# `scaffold` what the block was compiled with, as `--list-scaffold` names it,
#            or `-` for nothing. The scaffold is part of the claim a row makes.
# `ref`      the commit the block was measured BUILT at.
# THE LIST MUST EQUAL THE BUILT SET, in both directions (AC9, P0-4). A row for
# a block that no longer builds, or no longer exists, fails the gate; so does
# a block that builds and has no row. The second is what makes this a ratchet:
# a repair that makes a block build lands its row in the same PR.
# Admitted in phase 3 with NO PAGE EDITED: only blocks that build against the
# pin as the page prints them, given their page's scaffold. Blocks that need a
# `using` on the page belong to phase 4 or to backlog item 2.
